# R335 — Prefill Dm low-precision capacity audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Source-only audit at W HEAD 769ff3f11133a972bb9f7a78bb4a4cf52d52dcaf. Consulted R333, R301, R289 and R331 plus current Prefill sources. No project edit, build, test, import, project execution, GPU/profiler/process work, Git operation, cleanup, active-record access, or in-flight packet inspection. No local runtime, capacity, retransfers, or quality result was measured.

## Finding

A 16-bit Dm is a plausible capacity experiment, but it is not yet established that it enlarges a chunk or removes expert retransfers. Current Dm costs exactly 4*T*K*N bytes. With K=10 and N=2,560, that is 102,400*T bytes (100 KiB per prompt row); BF16/FP16 would save 51,200*T bytes (50 KiB per row), before alignment. At T=12,288 this is 1,200 MiB current and 600 MiB saved. At T=32,768 it would save 1,600 MiB. That is a material absolute amount.

However, Prefill reserves one shared region as max(GDN workspace, QSA workspace, MoE workspace), then carves each of those layouts over the same base. Dm is only one term in MoE. Even when MoE is the maximum, reducing Dm changes the region only by the lesser of the byte saving and the MoE margin above the next-largest GDN/QSA region. It changes no outer workspace allocation when GDN or QSA dominates, and it does not by itself prove the allocator, memory high-water, or chunk policy can use the difference to increase T. A larger T could reduce repeated whole-model expert walks, but that remains conditional on a capacity limit being relieved and on the next chunk size actually being admitted.

## Exact source accounting and path coverage

The source's moe_set_bytes and Prefill::init both allocate float[T*K*N] for Dm. bytes_needed_impl counts the shared max with the same MoE calculator. The regular and compact MoE allocation paths leave Dm at route capacity even if each compact expert has at most T rows. For each unit of T, Dm is 102,400 bytes; a 16-bit allocation is 51,200*T bytes.

Current down-output producers all need a coordinated format change:

- Non-MMQ/native path dequantizes a native expert's down weights to FP16 and computes grouped or individual down GEMMs into Dm as FP32. The XMX grouped and fallback calls receive float* output; the NativeDequantBatch1 route changes weight preparation, not the Dm element contract. A narrow eligible candidate should bind to the actual free-XMX NativeDequantBatch1 IQ3_S predicate and retain FP32 GEMM accumulation. If that route's writer is changed, verify all other native/non-native down call sites remain FP32 or are separately opted in.
- MMQ products carry float* dst; main grouped products, helper products, and remote-group output destinations write Dm or Dm_b. MMQ group output may exceed T rows, so the compact T*N staging idea from R301 is not a general fix. MMQ needs its own store epilogue and scratch accounting.
- Generic fused Q2_0 and native fused-IQ paths write Dm inside fused kernels and require kernel-level store variants.
- Peer-MMQ uses FP32 Dm_b double buffers or FP32 staging/copies before primary Dm. Dtype must cover those buffers, offsets, copy byte counts and conversion order.
- CPU expert product is not a Dm writer in the audited caller.

The common reader is moe_combine: ten route slots are loaded in rank order, multiplied by FP32 route weights and accumulated with FP32 FMA, then combined with the shared-expert term. Supporting Dm16 therefore requires converting each load to float in both scalar and vectorized combine kernels, and updating the NaN diagnostic that currently reads all Dm elements as float. Preserve FP32 accumulation; casting the stored expert result still rounds each expert contribution before weighting, and the later sum cannot recover those bits. The live window is the down products through combine only; SessionState KV, GDN and PLE state are separate persistent owners and must not be included in this candidate.

## Conditional candidate and gate

The smallest useful candidate is one dtype per arm (BF16 and FP16 separately), restricted to single-GPU free-XMX NativeDequantBatch1 IQ3_S, with no MMQ, fused route, peer output, or CPU MoE. Keep FP32 accumulators. Before implementation, pin the actual caller's runtime eligibility condition and route census field for that exact path; the source audit must show the predicate implies every Dm writer for the selected run uses the updated writer and every final read uses the matching Dm16 combine. If any other layer/path writes into the same Dm during that run, either cover it or reject the run. This is necessary because a global Dm dtype is shared across all MoE layers.

The candidate has an exact capacity prediction: recompute GDN, QSA, and MoE byte totals at each tested T; report the max before and after, and show whether Dm was on the critical MoE limb and whether the shared max moved. Record the admitted old/new chunk, allocator/high-water and streamed expert bytes/counts. Only those measurements can establish that a larger chunk avoided repeated expert transfers; the formula alone cannot.

R301 already documented the multi-producer/consumer hazards and candidate-local quality benchmark, so this finding adds the exact shared-region/chunk-bound arithmetic rather than proposing another generic Dm change. R331 sets the relevant quality interpretation: fixed-history full-logit comparisons can measure numerical drift, but there is no universal acceptable KL/NLL/PPL margin; task behavior and operational correctness remain separate gates. Use its comparator contract for a paired baseline/candidate capture, and report NLL delta, distribution metrics and deterministic task checks for this Dm boundary. Neither published intermediate precision examples nor another state tensor's results substitute for this exact route.

## External implementation evidence (analogy only)

The upstream llama.cpp MoE matrix multiply API allocates an F32 destination for routed MUL_MAT_ID, and its CPU expert kernel explicitly labels destination as F32: [llama.cpp loader](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/llama-model-loader.cpp), [CPU routed matmul kernel](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-et/et-kernels/src/mul_mat_id_f32.c). This is evidence that a mature inference implementation commonly retains FP32 routed projection outputs; it is not proof that Dm16 cannot work here, nor quality evidence for this model. vLLM documentation's explicit FP8 KV-cache dtype is a persistent-cache storage option, not evidence about a transient MoE output tensor; it is therefore not a close precedent for Dm. No primary source found in this audit quantifies quality for storing this model's MoE down outputs in BF16 or FP16.

## Decision

Keep Dm FP32 for the current qualified path. Treat route-restricted Dm16 as a worthwhile measured candidate only if the shared-region ledger shows Dm materially controls an allocation/admission limit at the intended chunk. The source-only byte arithmetic supports “potentially material saving”; it does not support “will enlarge chunks,” “will avoid expert retransfers,” or any quality claim.
